escena: SCENE (Efeonce office, Santiago, high floor, late morning): the Efeonce meeting room named «Responder.», from the chair at its table, seen from the chair of someone sitting there on a video call — camera at SEATED EYE LEVEL (about 1.15 m), 28 mm lens at f/5.6, like a good webcam view, looking straight at a matte dark-navy painted wall 2.5 m away; horizon level, verticals straight. RIGHT THIRD: Image 2 is the final artwork of that part of the wall — the room name «Responder» with its blue sphere as the period and, under it, a tall portrait whiteboard with the handwritten question, a small handwritten header, the three handwritten tool names and their tally marks. Reproduce Image 2 exactly as real materials: the room name as cut matte white vinyl letters with an azure vinyl dot; a real glossy enamel whiteboard with a slim aluminium frame and marker tray; the writing in real dry-erase marker with slightly uneven strokes. LEFT THIRD: beside a slim black-framed glass door at the left edge, a small wall-mounted room booking panel at eye height — a slim tablet in a black bezel whose screen shows Image 3 exactly (the room name, the filled status sphere and «En sesión»), glowing softly. At the bottom LEFT corner of the table, a current-generation thin laptop open at an angle, its screen showing Image 4 (a dashboard with the Efeonce AEO logo in its header), slightly out of focus. At the bottom RIGHT corner of the table, the official Efeonce logo from Image 1 as a small solid DEEP NAVY (#023C70, dark ink blue, never royal blue) desk object about 24 cm wide and 6 cm tall, standing upright on the table between 74% and 94% of the frame width, turned towards the camera: product placement, reproduced exactly (every letter of «efeonce», the ship emblem with its orbit ring, its cuts and its three small windows), satin finish, crisp bevel, its long hard shadow falling to the left. At the far RIGHT edge, floor-to-ceiling glazing shows the bright open office and the Andes far away in haze. LIGHT: hard, low late-morning sun from the RIGHT crosses the room as crisp visible shafts through the haze and rakes across the room name and the whiteboard with sharp mullion shadows; the centre of the wall stays in calm, even shade. TRACES OF WORK: a dry-erase marker with its cap off on the whiteboard tray; a graphite mesh chair pushed back at an angle below the board. MODERN FLOOR (2026, premium technology company): floor-to-ceiling glazing with slim black frames; smooth exposed concrete ceiling with recessed black linear LED profiles switched off; seamless pale microcement floor; furniture with clean lines — pale solid-surface or light-oak tables on slim black steel legs, graphite ergonomic mesh chairs, handle-less storage; current-generation technology only. At most ONE sculptural plant in the whole frame. Nothing vintage or rustic: no reclaimed wood, no brass, no Edison bulbs, no wooden brackets, no clutter. Nothing else on the walls: no posters, no clocks, no extra signage and no extra text anywhere. TEXT EXCEPTION: the logo from Image 1 and the artworks from Image 2, Image 3 and Image 4 are the ONLY readable marks in the picture; they stay crisp and legible, every letter and word exactly as in the references, never blurred, altered or translated; every other screen, paper or label stays illegible by physical means.
